questions.source_name: Textbook extract · Illustration 06
questions.stem: A particle of mass $m$ is moving in a circular path of constant radius $r$ such that its centripetal acceleration $a_c$ varies with time $t$ as $a_c = k^2 r t^2$, where $k$ is a constant. The power delivered to the particle by the net force acting on it is:

hints.prompt: Hint 1
hints.text: Centripetal acceleration is not necessarily the entire acceleration.

hints.prompt: Hint 2
hints.text: Separate the component perpendicular to velocity from the component changing its magnitude.

steps: From a_c = v²/r, infer v² = k²r²t² and (for nonnegative speed) v = |k|rt.
Radial force does no work; tangential acceleration changes the speed.
P = d(½mv²)/dt = mk²r²t.
questions.check: K = ½ m k²r²t², hence dK/dt = mk²r²t.

questions.source_name: Textbook extract · Illustration 11
questions.stem: A uniform flexible chain of length $l$ and mass $m$ overhangs a smooth horizontal table with two-thirds ($2l/3$) of its length lying on the table. Find the kinetic energy of the chain as it completely slips off the table.

hints.prompt: Hint 1
hints.text: Track the chain’s distributed mass, not a single point at one height.

hints.prompt: Hint 2
hints.text: Check whether the initial kinetic energy is stated.

questions.answer: Conditional on initial rest and the ideal-chain model: Kfinal = (4/9)mgl.
steps: Use linear density m/l and table-height gravitational reference.
Initial hanging length = l/3 gives U_initial = -mgl/18; completely hanging gives U_final = -mgl/2.
If initially at rest, K_final = U_initial - U_final = (4/9)mgl.
questions.check: Initial hanging mass m/3 is at depth l/6: U_i = -(m/3)g(l/6).
flags: Stem does not expressly specify initial kinetic energy; 4mgl/9 is conditional on release from rest and an ideal inextensible chain.

questions.source_name: Textbook extract · Illustration 12
questions.stem: A block of mass $m$ is pushed against a light spring of spring constant $k$ fixed at one end to a rigid vertical wall. The block slides on a frictionless horizontal table. The natural length of the spring is $L_0$. The spring is compressed to half its natural length ($x_{\text{init}} = L_0/2$) and the block is released from rest. Find the velocity of the block as a function of its distance $x$ from the wall.
questions.figure_note: Illustrative author schematic, not verified against printed textbook illustration.

hints.prompt: Hint 1
hints.text: Being pushed against a spring does not mean being permanently attached.

hints.prompt: Hint 2
hints.text: Identify where the contact force can cease.

questions.answer: During contact: v(x) = √[(k/m)(L₀²/4 − (L₀ − x)²)] for L₀/2 ≤ x ≤ L₀. After detachment: v = (L₀/2)√(k/m).
steps: Initial spring energy equals kL₀²/8.
For L₀/2 ≤ x ≤ L₀, the spring remains in contact and stores ½k(L₀−x)².
At x = L₀ the spring reaches natural length and block detaches; its speed then remains constant.
questions.check: v(L₀/2)=0 and v(L₀)=(L₀/2)√(k/m); do not extrapolate the contact formula beyond x=L₀.
flags: The block is pressed against, not attached to, the spring. Contact ends at natural length; one spring-energy expression must not be extended past detachment.

questions.source_name: Synthetic engineering control (not Core2 source evidence)
questions.stem: An idealised trolley moves horizontally while a constant force acts vertically. What is the work done by this force on the trolley during the horizontal displacement?
options: Not enough information about the speed

hints.prompt: Hint 1
hints.text: Focus on the work by the specified force, not the net work.

hints.prompt: Hint 2
hints.text: Compare the force and displacement directions.

questions.answer: C — Zero work by the vertical force.
steps: Work by a constant force is F · s.
The vertical force and horizontal displacement are perpendicular.
Therefore this force does zero work, irrespective of trolley speed.
questions.check: The same force does zero work over twice the horizontal distance.
